item.title: Gouverner par les comptes ? Comptabilité, accountability et transformations de la gouvernance
item.content:encoded:
François Aubert,

Emmanuelle Dubocage,

Célia Lemaire,

Sébastien Rocher,

Vanessa Serret,

Bérangère Szostak,

Cette journée de recherche interroge les interactions entre comptabilité, accountability et gouvernance organisationnelle. Elle dépasse une conception de la comptabilité comme simple technique d'information pour analyser comment les comptes, indicateurs et reportings façonnent activement les structures de gouvernance et les rapports de pouvoir, tandis que les systèmes de gouvernance déterminent ce qui doit être mesuré et rapporté.

La journée répond à des enjeux contemporains : élargissement de l'accountability au-delà des actionnaires vers une pluralité de parties prenantes, développement du reporting de durabilité, et gouvernance croissante par les nombres et les algorithmes. Elle accueille des recherches quantitatives, qualitatives ou mixtes dans tous les types d'organisations, avec un accent particulier sur les études théorisant explicitement les interactions entre ces trois domaines.

Appel publié par Finance Contrôle Stratégie. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Comptabilité, accountability et architecture de la gouvernance
  • Élargissement de l'accountability et pluralité des parties prenantes
  • Reporting financier et extra-financier
  • Gouvernance par les nombres : indicateurs et performance
  • Transformations technologiques de la comptabilité et de la gouvernance
  • Intelligence artificielle et reddition des comptes
  • Gouvernance des données et algorithmes

item.title: Implementing the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive: Challenges, Opportunities, and Emerging Practices
item.content:encoded:
Diogenis Baboukardos, Audencia Business School

Begoña Giner, Universitat de València

Ronita Ram, University of Reading

Frank Schiemann, University of Bamberg

The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), adopted by the European Union in 2022, represents a major transformation in corporate sustainability disclosure regulation. The directive expands the scope of affected companies, introduces European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) covering environmental, social, and governance topics, and mandates third-party assurance. However, these changes present significant implementation challenges for companies, assurance providers, and information users. In 2025, the EU proposed amendments through an 'Omnibus' package aiming to simplify reporting requirements and reduce compliance burdens, though these changes have created uncertainty and raised concerns about potentially weakening the EU's sustainability leadership.

Appel publié par Accounting in Europe. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • The role of CSRD/ESRS to fulfil investors and other stakeholders' needs and be a strategic mechanism to enhance Europe's competitiveness, resilience, and capacity for innovation
  • Implementation challenges: Practical hurdles or burdens faced by companies in adopting CSRD/ESRS, including data collection, stakeholder engagement, and materiality assessment
  • Benefits of the EU transparency disclosure framework: The economic, operational, and reputational effects of CSRD/ESRS implementation
  • Interactions and alignment between ESRS and global frameworks: How ESRS aligns (or conflicts) with other frameworks, such as GRI or IFRS S1 & S2, and the implications, especially for multinational companies
  • Regulatory, institutional, and political dynamics: Institutional and political forces impacting the CSRD's evolution, including the role of EFRAG and EU member states
  • Sector-specific disclosure challenges: Unique hurdles and burdens faced by different sectors, such as finance, energy, manufacturing, or technology, in meeting CSRD requirements
  • Implications of CSRD for audit firms and assurance providers: The evolving role of auditors, the requirements for the development of assurance standards, and the impacts of the CSRD/Omnibus on the capacity of the assurance market to meet demand
  • Implications of CSRD for small and medium-sized enterprises and non-European companies: Direct and indirect effects of the CSRD/Omnibus on small and medium-sized enterprises and non-EU firms operating in or trading with the EU
  • Comparative perspectives: Variations in CSRD implementation across EU member states, including differences in national enforcement
  • Critical perspectives: Risks of greenwashing, standard overload, and compliance-driven reporting, as well as (threats to) the potential for the CSRD to drive meaningful sustainability outcomes
  • CSRD impact beyond the EU: CSRD's influence on sustainability reporting regulation and practices in non-EU countries and its role in shaping global standards

Timeline

  • September 1, 2026: Submission open date
  • November 30, 2026: Manuscript deadline
